title: Midnight staggered rollout notes (personal)
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad for a midnight staggered rollout (NA -> EU -> APAC) of model-serving v2.8.3 with version pinning and gradual traffic shaping. Not a formal runbook yet — for working through sequence, signals, and fallbacks.

Context:
- Model family: rw-chat-13b (quantized q4f16) -> v2.8.3 (perf kernels + small tokenizer change)
- Goal: push to hosted and dedicated pools with minimal user-visible regressions and clear rollback path.
- Constraint: APAC region has lower spare capacity at midnight window; prefer slower ramp there.

High-level plan (UTC times):
- T-02:00 -> preflight smoke on internal test org (0% production traffic)
- T+00:00 -> NA warmup cohort (0.5% of prod traffic, 20k tokens/min) for 30m
- T+00:30 -> NA increase -> 5% for 1h (observe p95 and error rate)
- T+02:00 -> EU warmup 0.5% for 30m, then 5% for 1h
- T+05:00 -> APAC slow drip 0.1% -> 1% -> 3% over 3h (watch saturation)
- T+09:00 -> global 25% canary if all signals green
- Roll to 100% via step-ups tied to infra metrics and eval set quality checks (see Post-launch).

Cohort selection rules:
- Prefer stable clients: non-beta apps, >90th percentile request success historically, pre-identified client ids (cohort list in INF-4129).
- Exclude latency-sensitive partners until we hit 5% regionally.
- Sticky cookie: route returning users to same variant for at least 24h.

Pinning and fallback details:
- Model pin: set model_alias "rw-chat-13b:stable-202603" -> points to v2.8.3 for canary cohorts.
- Fallbacks: configured fallback chain: rw-chat-13b:q4f16-v2.7.0 -> rw-chat-13b:int8-backup. If kernel error or OOM, automatically route to previous stable.
- Client-level pin overrides allowed for enterprise customers via feature-flag. Documented in linked PR.

Preflight checklist (quick):
- [ ] Merge runtime PR (GH#987) and tag image: redwood/runtime:2026-03-10-v2.8.3
- [ ] Canary config uploaded to infra (ticket INF-4129)
content_2: - [ ] Load test: 5m closed-loop at target p95 load on dedicated pool (use loadtest worker set B)
content_3: - [ ] Run eval harness on regression prompt set (small subset) and compare top-1 pass rate (tolerance < 0.8% regression)
content_4:
- [ ] Healthcheck probes: token failure, decode errors, kv-cache misses instrumented
- [ ] Alerting ready: P95 latency > 2s, request_error_rate > 0.5% (5m), hallucination-alert if eval spike > threshold

Observability queries (promql examples):
- error rate (all): sum(rate(redwood_inference_request_errors_total[5m])) by (region) / sum(rate(redwood_inference_requests_total[5m])) by (region)
- p95 latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, region))
- kv cache hit ratio: sum(rate(redwood_kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) / sum(rate(redwood_kv_cache_requests_total[5m]))

Quick health scripts / commands (notes):
- redwoodctl rollout start --model rw-chat-13b --version v2.8.3 --cohort na-warmup --percent 0.5
- redwoodctl rollout step --cohort na-warmup --to 5
- redwoodctl rollback --model rw-chat-13b --to-version v2.7.0 --reason "auto-fallback: p95 breach"
- kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=runtime | grep v2.8.3  # double-check nodes draining

Rollback criteria (automatic/manual):
- auto: region-level request_error_rate > 0.7% sustained 10m OR p95 > 2.5x stable baseline for 5m
- manual: output-quality regression flagged by eval harness > 1.0% absolute drop on key prompts OR customer complaint from tier-1 support

Post-launch evals and sanity checks:
- Run full regression suite (1000 prompts) after hitting 25% for 2h; if delta > tolerance, plan immediate rollback and postmortem.
- Spot-check hallucination keywords list (appendix) against new outputs.
content_5:
- [ ] Re-run small eval after merge and paste results here

Scratch / brain dump (messy):
- If we do sticky cookie routing, need to verify cookie TTL across CDNs; otherwise users could flip between versions and confound metrics.
- Consider backoff policy: if error spikes then cut 50% immediately, otherwise step-down 2x less aggressive than roll-up.
- For APAC, maybe do 0.05% -> 0.2% -> 1% steps given capacity. Might be too slow but safer.
- One-liner alert message for pager duty: "Canary v2.8.3 p95 breach in <region> — consider rollback or throttle"

End of scratchpad. Will clean up and extract formal runbook after a dry run.

-- Taylor
